runs.text:
Millbrook Hollow's city council voted on Tuesday night to approve an amended parks-and-recreation budget line, at a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. The new figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, said a spokesperson for the mayor's office, who declined to elaborate. A memo from the finance subcommittee, seen by two council staffers, put the adjustment at roughly $340,000—a sum one budget analyst called "in the range we expected."

Near the bottom of that memo, and unmentioned by any council member during the meeting, was a more urgent line: the bridge's lead structural engineer has found a load-bearing crack serious enough to require closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project has sat on the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already racked up 14 change orders. It went undiscussed. Asked afterward for comment, council member Dana Okafor said only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
